_readme: Adjudications that DIFFER from what the committed artifact records.
An artifact captures what an agent concluded at the time. Where the
maintainer later overruled that conclusion, the file was never updated — so
backfilling it mechanically would write the opposite of the record. Each
entry below cites the CLAUDE.md Decisions-log date carrying the real outcome.
Key format: <pipeline>/<artifactId>::<ref>, where artifactId is the filename
up to the first dot. That is DELIBERATELY coarse: NCERT Integrals is split
artifactId 'integrals', so one adjudication covers every artifact describing
the same ref. Ex 7.9 Q9 is exactly that case — it appears in both a
cross-check and a blind mcq-verify, and both should record the same verdict.
Unmatched keys are reported by the backfill as a BLOCKING error, so a stale

ncert/integrals::Ex 7.9 Q9.note: [Backfill adjudication, Decisions log 2026-07-11] The artifact records OUR-ANSWER-WRONG and recommended flipping our (A) to the NCERT key (D). That was OVERTURNED: the cross-check agent had options:[] from a dump-review field-name bug, and reading the printed page shows our (A)=6 is correct while the NCERT key contradicts its own printed options. Our answer stands; the book key is the defect.

stateboard/trig-functions-12::Misc I Q.1.note: [Backfill adjudication, Decisions log 2026-07-06] Defective question: the true solution nπ/3 is not among the printed options. The blind derivation reports A; the official key is B (via 6θ=nπ), which the bank deliberately retains so the row matches the board. Recorded as a source defect, not as a disagreement to resolve.

_comment: The ten entries below resolve a VERDICT CONFLICT, not a stale artifact.
NCERT Ex 7.8 Q13-22 sit in two overlapping agent batches of the same
cross-check. integrals.ex678 recorded CANT-READ-KEY ('the reprint lists
Ex 7.8 answers 1-12 only'); integrals.ex8910 recorded AGREE and, for all
ten, transcribed a concrete printed book_key — i.e. it located the key
under the old Exercise 7.9 numbering, exactly as the other batch
hypothesised it might sit. Seven match our answer verbatim; the other
three (Q16, Q17, Q20) are trivial equivalences, each verified by hand:
Q16 distributes to ours, Q17 is term reordering, Q20 is
4/pi - 2sqrt2/pi = (4-2sqrt2)/pi. Evidence beats absence of evidence, so
all ten are confirmed. Without these entries the dedupe constraint would
have let readdir order pick a winner - which is how the first backfill
run silently stored the weaker verdict.
